beats.text: The network between your machines breaks...
beats.say: Your database runs on many machines. What happens when the network between them breaks?

beats.text: Pick two: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.
beats.say: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can guarantee only two of three: consistency, availability, and partition tolerance. And since networks do fail, partition tolerance is not optional.

beats.text: A write lands on A. Then the link breaks.
beats.say: Say a write lands on node A, and then the link breaks. Node B never gets the update, so it still holds the old value.

beats.text: CP: refuse to answer. Consistent, not available.
beats.say: A C P system refuses to answer on node B, to avoid serving stale data. It stays consistent, but unavailable.

beats.text: AP: answer anyway. Available, maybe stale.
beats.say: An A P system answers anyway, with the old value. It stays available, but may be inconsistent.

beats.text: It's a tradeoff. Pick for your use case.
beats.say: Banks choose consistency. Social feeds choose availability. It's always a tradeoff.
